newsitem.title: USA: Merix sees Q2 sales off 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Merix sees Q2 sales off 15 pct.

text.p: Merix Corp on Monday said that, based on a review of quarter-to-date results for its second fiscal quarter ending November 30, 1996, sales will be about 15 percent below the prior fiscal quarter.
As a result of this shortfall in sales, the company said in a statement it expects to be near break-even this quarter.
In the first quarter, Merix reported a profit of $1.26 million, or $0.20 a share, on sales of $41.1 million.
According to First Call the company was expected to report second quarter profits of about $0.13 a share, down from $0.45 a year ago.
"Orders from some of our major customers are substantially below original estimates," Debi Coleman, chief executive and chairman of Merix said.
"We believe that the impact of lower orders has been magnified by our high customer concentration. Adding new customers remains our top priority."

Merix is a manufacturer of technologically advanced electronic interconnect solutions, including rigid circuit boards, flexible and rigid-flex circuits, high-performance circuits and backplanes for use in sophisticated electronic equipment.
